subject: SIG: encryption lifecycle — KMS/HSM rotation details & evidence
messages:
From: lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SIG – follow-up: encryption key rotation evidence and custody

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking SIG ownership on this. Acme's security review team needs clarification and evidence for a few SIG questions around encryption and key custody before we can finalize the assessment. Can you please provide the following items or point us to where we can download them? Ideally by end of week but happy to extend if you need more time.

1) High-level statement of encryption in transit and at rest for Redwood-hosted models (protocols, TLS versions, cipher suites).
2) KMS/HSM architecture diagram and list of providers in production (e.g., AWS KMS, CloudHSM, on-prem HSM vendor).
3) Key rotation policy and actual rotation logs for the last 12 months (KEK and DEK rotation cadence, emergency rotation procedures).
4) Evidence of HSM certification (FIPS level) and cert chain.
5) Confirmation whether customers can use BYOK/Bring-Your-Own-Key and how key separation/multi-tenancy is enforced.

Attachments that would help: rotation logs, an HSM cert (PDF), and a completed SIG matrix. We prefer CSV/PDF/XLSX.

If there's a single place you prefer to upload these (Drive/DocuSign/secure portal), please share the link.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Security Operations
Acme Corporation

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG – follow-up: encryption key rotation evidence and custody

Lena — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you requested. Proposed plan:

- Rishi will pull rotation logs and the CSV export for the last 12 months (KEK/DEK events).
- Kimberly will assemble the policy boilerplate and confirm BYOK semantics and tenancy controls.
- Dylan will attach the HSM certificate chain and a short architecture diagram for KMS/HSM interaction.

I'll compile a single evidence bundle and upload it to a shared Drive folder. Timeline: preliminary bundle by EOD Thursday (2026-11-18), final by Monday if we need additional redactions. If that works for you we'll proceed.

Quick answers up front: encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred; at rest we use AES-256-GCM for data keys with envelope encryption via KMS-managed keys. More detail in the bundle.

Internal notes: assigning ticket SEC-4521 for tracking.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: james.holt@auditinsights.io
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-17T10:23:00-08:00
Subject: RE: SIG – follow-up: encryption key rotation evidence and custody

Mina / Lena,

Quick clarifying question from the audit team: for KEK wrapping we need to know the algorithms used for key wrapping and whether your HSMs are configured to enforce only approved algorithms (e.g., RSA-OAEP-SHA256, AES-KW). Also can you confirm the FIPS level of the HSMs in use and whether the certificate chain includes the HSM vendor root cert?

Separately, could you state the maximum rotation window for a data encryption key (DEK) and whether rotations are automated (and logged) or manual? We will note automation where present.

Thanks — James Holt
Senior Auditor, AuditInsights

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com, james.holt@auditinsights.io
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG – follow-up: encryption key rotation evidence and custody (evidence bundle)

Hi Lena / James —

Thanks for the patience. We uploaded a focused evidence bundle to the Drive link below and included short answers to the SIG encryption items you asked about. If you want a formal flattened SIG matrix we can return that as an XLSX next.

Drive bundle: https://drive.google.com/fake/redwood/sig-evidence-20261116
Files included (attached to this email and in Drive):
- redwood-kms-rotation-log-2026.csv (CSV export of rotation events and key IDs, 11/2025–11/2026)
- hsm-cert-chain.pdf (vendor cert chain and FIPS attestation excerpts)
- sig-evidence-collection-index.xlsx (index and mappings to SIG questions)

Short answers (high level):
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 enforced; we avoid weak ciphers (ECDHE + AES-GCM preferred). Mutual TLS is used for inter-service control-plane RPCs; external API endpoints use standard client-server TLS.
- Encryption at rest: Data encrypted with per-tenant data encryption keys (DEKs) using AES-256-GCM. DEKs are wrapped with a key encryption key (KEK) stored in KMS/HSM.
- KMS/HSM architecture: Production uses AWS KMS for KEK lifecycle and AWS CloudHSM for customer-managed HSM-backed keys where customers opt into BYOK. We also support an on-prem HSM integration option (Thales) for private deployments. Diagram is in the Drive bundle.
- HSM certification: CloudHSM instances are FIPS 140-2 Level 2 certified; on-prem Thales HSMs are FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (see hsm-cert-chain.pdf). The certificate chain and vendor attestations are included.
- Key wrapping algorithms & crypto policy: We use AES-KW (RFC 3394) for symmetric wrapping and RSA-OAEP-SHA256 for asymmetric wrap where applicable. HSM policies are hardened to only allow approved mechanisms; vendor root certs are present in the cert chain we provided.
- Rotation cadence and automation:
  - DEKs: rotated automatically on a 90-day cadence by default; rotation events are logged in the KMS audit stream and the rotation CSV.
  - KEKs (master/wrapping keys): rotated on a 12-month cadence or upon planned key compromise. Manual emergency rotation procedures are documented; emergency rotations trigger immediate logging and a change-control entry in SEC-4521.
  - Customer-managed BYOK: customers may bring their own keys via CloudHSM or external KMS; rotation cadence for BYOK keys is the customer's responsibility but we provide rotation tooling and recommended policies in the integration guide.
- Multi-tenancy and separation: DEKs are scoped per-tenant and namespaced in the KMS; access controls (IAM + RBAC) prevent cross-tenant key access. Key material for different tenants never shares the same DEK.
- Evidence provenance and logs: rotation events, KMS audit trails, and operator actions are exported to our secure logging pipeline and retained per our data retention policy. The CSV contains key IDs, event timestamps, actor (service principal or human operator), and rotation reason.

Next steps: if you'd like a redacted flattened SIG matrix (XLSX) flagged with row-level evidence links, we can produce that by EOD Monday. Let us know if you need any additional artifacts or deeper crypto proofs (e.g., HSM key ceremony notes).

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
